facts.claim: Everest: highest point on Earth; summit rocks are uplifted ocean sediments full of marine fossils
Summit elevation: 8,849 m (29,032 ft), on the Nepal–China (Tibet) border
Summit: winds over 160 km/h (100 mph), regularly below −30°C (−22°F), about a third of sea-level oxygen
Still rising: about 2 mm (0.08 in) per year, which fits the Indian plate still subducting
Why Everest is the tallest and not a nearby peak: probably “just luck”
Neotethys Ocean: closed by subduction before the Indian and Eurasian plates collided
Collision: began 50–60 million years ago
Plates still converging: 40–50 mm per year
Subduction: uneven; Indian crust slides under southern Tibet
Mantle flow: slow, driven by interior heat; it moves the plates
Interior heat: keeps plate tectonics going, which shapes Earth’s surface over billions of years
“Cold curtains”: cold sheets of material sink into the deep interior, like subducted slabs
Plate motion: can change abruptly; in a convection model, a reorganization took about 6–8 million years

facts.claim: Earth’s interior: crust, mantle, liquid outer core, solid inner core

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Crust: about 0–100 km deep

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Crust beneath the Tibetan Plateau: twice the global average thickness

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Base of the crust under the Himalayan collision zone: about 66–81 km deep

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Crust under Everest: probably near its maximum thickness; any taller and the mountain may sink

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Mantle: down to 2,900 km; seismic discontinuity at 410 km; lower mantle from 670 km

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Minerals: 410 km boundary tied to olivine changing to wadsleyite; inclusions in a 420–440 km diamond: garnet, 10-Å phase, ilmenite, liebermannite

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Outer core: liquid iron-nickel

facts.section: Earth’s layers, structure, composition and minerals
facts.claim: Inner core boundary: 5,100 km depth
Temperature: rises with depth
Earth’s heat: left over from its formation, plus the decay of radioactive isotopes such as potassium
Bottom of tectonic plates (up to 200 km deep): 1,300–1,500°C
410 km discontinuity: about 1,560°C
Top of the lower mantle (670 km): about 1,700°C
Base of the mantle (2,900 km): about 2,300°C; outer core: about 3,700°C
Inner core boundary (5,100 km): about 6,000°C, close to the Sun’s surface temperature
